meaning: possessive particle, links a noun to its modifier
core: 的 marks that what comes before belongs to or describes what comes after. Learners often forget it or put it in the wrong place — in spoken Mandarin it is nearly always needed between a person and their thing.

sentences.situation: At a café · to a friend
sentences.pinyin: zhè bēi kāfēi shì wǒ de
sentences.en: This cup of coffee is mine.
sentences.why: You point to your cup among several on the table and tell your friend whose it is. 的 here turns 我 into 'mine'.
sentences.tip: Stress 我 de lightly. Do not say 我咖啡 — that sounds like a product called 'me-coffee'.

sentences.en: Do you have any cheaper ones?
sentences.why: You are looking at prices and ask the assistant for items in a lower range. 的 after an adjective means 'the ones that are cheap'.
sentences.tip: Very common shopping phrase. Dropping 的 sounds abrupt and unnatural.

sentences.pinyin: nǐ de shǒujī zài zhuōzi shàng
sentences.en: Your phone is on the table.
sentences.why: You noticed your roommate left their phone behind and tell them where it is. 的 links 你 to 手机.
sentences.tip: In quick speech 你的 often softens to nǐ de; never drop the 的 here.

sentences.pinyin: míngtiān de huì jǐ diǎn kāishǐ
sentences.en: What time does tomorrow's meeting start?
sentences.why: You message a colleague to ask about the meeting scheduled for tomorrow. 的 links the time word 明天 to the noun 会.
sentences.tip: Time words need 的 before a noun: 明天的会, not 明天会 (which means 'will meet').

sentences.why: You share your proposal with your boss and frame it as your own view. 的 marks that the idea belongs to you.
sentences.tip: Slightly more deferential than 我觉得. Good for meetings.

sentences.pinyin: wǒ yào yí gè là de
sentences.why: At a noodle shop you order by taste instead of naming the dish. 的 turns the adjective 辣 into 'the spicy one'.
sentences.tip: Very natural in small restaurants. 一个辣的 = a spicy dish.

sentences.situation: On the phone · to a client
sentences.pinyin: zhè shì Wáng zǒng de yóuxiāng
sentences.en: This is Mr. Wang's email address.
sentences.why: You give a client your manager's contact. 的 links 王总 to 邮箱 — without it you would be saying 'Mr. Wang is an email address'.
sentences.tip: Always use 的 between a person and their thing, even with names.

sentences.why: You walk into a friend's newly decorated room and compliment them. 的 links 你 to 房间.
sentences.tip: Stress 真 to sound sincere, not flat.

sentences.pinyin: shīfu, zhè shì wǒ de dìzhǐ
sentences.why: You hand the driver your phone showing the destination. 的 links 我 to 地址.
sentences.tip: Calling a taxi driver 师傅 is standard and friendly in mainland China.

sentences.situation: Formal email · to a partner company
sentences.zh: 我们的产品价格很有优势。
sentences.pinyin: wǒmen de chǎnpǐn jiàgé hěn yǒu yōushì
sentences.en: Our product's price is very competitive.
sentences.why: In a business email you describe your company's pricing strength. 的 links 我们 to 产品.
sentences.tip: In writing, keep 的; in very casual speech you may say 我们产品 without it.

quiz.prompt: You are at a café and point to your cup. Tell your friend: 'This coffee is mine.'
quiz.explain: 的 after 我 means 'mine' and is the natural way to claim ownership.

quiz.prompt: You are shopping and ask the assistant: 'Do you have any cheaper ones?'
quiz.explain: 的 after an adjective means 'the ones that are cheap' — a standard shopping phrase.

quiz.prompt: Message your colleague: 'What time does tomorrow's meeting start?' Be natural and neutral.
quiz.explain: Time words like 明天 need 的 before a noun; without it 明天会 means 'will meet'.

quiz.prompt: You are at a noodle shop. Tell the waiter you want a spicy one. Sound direct and casual.
quiz.explain: 的 turns the adjective 辣 into 'the spicy one', the usual way to order by taste.

quiz.prompt: 朋友问：这是谁的手机？你回答：你的手机在桌子上。
quiz.explain: 的 links 你 to 手机; dropping it would change the meaning.

quiz.prompt: 客户问：这是王总的邮箱吗？你回答：对，这是王总的邮箱。
quiz.explain: A person's name always needs 的 before their thing, even in formal speech.
